text:
sara: heads-up — getting a batch of support escalations from eu2 customers, ~08:02 UTC. Symptoms: 502s from api-gateway, repeated 504 timeouts from hosted inference endpoints, and p95 token latency spikes. Multiple tenants across different AZs (eu2-a and eu2-b).

mike: support seeing 15+ tickets, some with reproducible 502s on POST /v1/generate. Customers report rapid retries still failing. Escalating to infra.

andre: looking at network metrics now. I'm seeing micro packet loss and jitter on the eu2-to-transit peering links starting ~07:58 UTC. BGP flaps observed on transit neighbor AS64512.

vinh: any host-level errors? load looks normal on inference fleet, no OOMs. Gateways show high connection resets. Here's a quick mtr from a gateway host to the transit next-hop:

```
Start: gateway-eu2-a-01
HOST: gateway-eu2-a-01  Loss%   Snt   Last   Avg  Best  Wrst StDev
 1.|-- 10.0.1.1            0.0%    20    0.4   0.6   0.3   2.1   0.4
 2.|-- 192.0.2.10         12.5%    20   15.8  20.3   1.2  110.5  30.2
 3.|-- 203.0.113.5        18.7%    20   22.1  25.9  20.8   60.2  12.9
 4.|-- 198.51.100.2        0.0%    20   25.0  24.2  22.9   27.5   1.1
```

vinh: you can see loss/jitter concentrated on hop 2/3 (transit edges).

andre: confirmed BGP churn in our peering session with AS64512 — 3 withdraws in 6 minutes. Provider's status page not yet updated. Opening provider incident now (TID 8472).

deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T08:10:05 by nina — rolled a small routing override to prefer partner-b for eu2-egress for canary pool (id: canary-65).

nina: quick mitigation: we injected a more-specific route to prefer partner-b for a subset of traffic to avoid the flapping peer. This is only for the hosted-api gateway subnet and is applied to canary first.

mike: passing mitigation note to affected customers. Some asked for guidance on retry/backoff. Suggested: exponential backoff with jitter, 504-handling, and avoid hammering. Adding support doc link: https://redwood.example.com/docs/retries

raj: customers asking about SLA credits. We need a clear statement — is this regional and transient?

andre: provider has acknowledged an anomaly on their peering fabric, assigned ticket P-5391. They report an upstream provider experiencing a partial circuit failure. ETA unknown. For now routing via partner-b reduces error rate for the canary.

vinh: actioned a broader reroute to partner-b for all hosted-api gateways in eu2 at 08:14 UTC after canary looked good. Monitoring for regressions.

mike: support update posted to customers at 08:20 UTC. Customers who had immediate needs offered temporary migration to eu1 or private/dedicated.

andre: quick diff of BGP logs showing withdraws:

```
2026-03-15T07:58:12Z - BGP: neighbor 203.0.113.1 ASN 64512 NOTIFICATION (update)
2026-03-15T08:01:02Z - BGP: 4 prefix withdraws from 64512
2026-03-15T08:03:45Z - BGP: session reset (neighbor flapped)
2026-03-15T08:07:29Z - BGP: session reestablished
```

nina: we toggled gateway connection keepalives and increased BGP dampening temporarily to reduce churn.

oncall: paging logs showed surge in alerts for gateway-conn-reset events at 07:59-08:05 UTC. Pager rotations oncall handled initial triage.

mike: ticket thread with enterprise customer ACME Corp — they reported repeated 504s during a demo. Escalation path activated; shared temporary workaround (route to eu1). They want ETA for full resolution.

vinh: current numbers after reroute: 502 rate down from 2.1% -> 0.3% and p95 latency back to baseline in ~6 minutes for canary. Still monitoring full fleet.

andre: provider pushed partial fix to peer fabric per P-5391 at 08:32 UTC, but recommended customers keep fallback routes in place while they complete repair.

nina: note for ops — we had a config that allowed cross-az egress stickiness causing some traffic to continue via problematic AS; we updated route selection to recompute next-hop sooner on BGP withdraws.

raj: sent a customer-facing timeline and promised follow-up email once provider confirms full repair.

vinh: open action items: (1) postmortem owner (andre), (2) run routing resilience runbook to add second peering in eu2 long-term, (3) add synthetic checks that validate path through both partners and alert if >5% loss on any path.

andre: assigning myself postmortem. I'll gather BGP dumps, netflow, and correlate impacted customer lists.

mike: closing loop with support: customers notified, some accepted temporary migrations. Will follow-up for SLA/billing asks after postmortem.

sara: thanks team. Current status: degraded -> partial mitigation in place via partner-b routing; provider acknowledged incident P-5391 and working on the fix. We'll keep this thread updated and move to a formal incident doc after postmortem. :white_check_mark:
